question: The diameter of a sphere made of copper is 3 cm. The sphere is melted and recast into a wire. If the length of the wire is half metre, then what is the diameter of the wire ?
solution:
**Given:**

The diameter of a sphere made of copper = 3 cm

Length of the wire (ℓ) = 1/2 m = 0.5 m = 50 cm

**Formula used:**

The volume of the sphere = (4)/(3)πR³

The volume of the cylinder = πr²h

Where,

R = Radius of the sphere

r = Radius of the cylinder

h = height of the cylinder

**Calculation:**

Since, R = (3)/(2) cm, 

Length of the wire (ℓ) = 50 cm 

Here, the height of the cylinder is the same as the length of the wire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/65b4ed74680b2357c22374147b84973f14035c2bc2653551b8e3c0486c3817b7.png] 

The volume of the sphere = volume of the cylinder

⇒ (4)/(3)πR3 = πr²h

⇒ (4)/(3) pi× ((3)/(2))³ = pi r²×50

⇒ (4)/(3) × (27)/(8)= 50 r² 

⇒ 9/2 = 50 r²

⇒ r² = 9/100 = 0.09

⇒** r = 0.3**

Hence, 

Diameter of wire = 0.3 × 2 = 0.6 cm

∴ The required diameter of the wire is 0.6 cm.
